findings.finding: strict hourly grid, no gaps, no missing cells
splits are chronological; target ranges do not overlap
fitted statistics equal the training rows [0, 8640) and differ measurably from the whole-series statistics
no row is a forecast target in more than one split

findings.evidence: first val window starts at row 8544, first val target at row 8640
findings.finding: validation and test inputs read up to 96 rows before their split boundary, which is upstream's design and is not leakage: those rows are inputs only, never targets, and never fitted on
early stopping and best-checkpoint are keyed on validation loss

test loss is evaluated and printed every epoch alongside validation loss. It does not enter early stopping or checkpoint selection, so it is not leakage in the code -- but it is a human-in-the-loop channel and has to be disclosed
the cycle index is a function of the row number alone (`(row + L) mod W`), so it cannot carry future values
the loader computes calendar features but TQNet's forward signature takes only (x, cycle_index), so they are never consumed

findings.evidence: denorm lines commented: True; every test channel crosses zero: True
findings.finding: de-normalisation is left commented out upstream, so MSE/MAE are in z-scored units, not degrees Celsius. This is why 0.3712 is the right order of magnitude, and why MAPE and SMAPE are unusable: the normalised series crosses zero in every channel
